quote.text: Far better an approximate answer to the right question, which is often vague, than an exact answer to the wrong question, which can always be made precise.
quote.author: John W. Tukey, “The Future of Data Analysis”, Annals of Mathematical Statistics (1962)

stories.headline: Two ministries, one set of teenagers, a thousand apart
stories.dek: Turnout fell by seventy-one per cent on the day the government gave way. One ministry counts who was seized in the street; the other counts who was held in a cell.

stories.kicker: The Rabbit Hole · Ten Metres, Half a Millimetre
stories.headline: The hardest target in sport is a white dot
stories.dek: An air-rifle ten-ring is half a millimetre across at ten metres. The men’s air-pistol qualification record has stood since 2009 — and in Singapore the gun has to live at the club.

stories.headline: A country ran out of dollars, so it made land
stories.dek: Reserves halved in a single month in April. Five months later the Maldives put five hundred hectares that did not exist in 2023 on the market — on terms its own attorney-general says are not yet an agreement.

stories.kicker: Singapore · The Haze on Race Friday
stories.headline: The reading doubled while the forecast stayed the same
stories.dek: All five regions were Unhealthy at five this morning, with the West at 171 overnight. The agency’s published outlook has used the same three words since Sunday.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Mattresses and Slat Bases
stories.headline: Four famous names, one Spanish company
stories.dek: The coil count on the label is, in the specialists’ own words, among the worst ways to buy a bed. The number that would tell you something is almost never printed.

stories.headline: Two numbers, and everything that explains them is a guess
stories.dek: Samsung guided to its first quarter above a hundred trillion won. Its preliminary filing contains no segment breakdown at all, so the phone division’s loss exists only as somebody’s estimate.

stories.headline: The earbud that cannot say whether it has a battery
stories.dek: Ninety-nine US dollars, a USB-C plug and no charging — except in the specification table, which says it is rechargeable and ships a charger.

stories.kicker: The Good Life · Bremont’s Blue Ceramic
stories.headline: The dearest one is the one nobody called limited
stories.dek: Three magazines printed a 250-piece edition on Wednesday. Bremont’s own shop prints no limitation at all — on a page where the cheaper white model says 150.

stories.headline: Two scores, one film, and a review count nobody prints
stories.dek: The Social Reckoning opens today on sixty-one per cent from a hundred and twenty critics — and fifty-three from forty-five. Every weekend figure in circulation is a forecast.

stories.kicker: The Family Desk · The Threshold At Twelve
stories.headline: She crossed a line in July and no letter came
stories.dek: Singapore’s paediatric advice says under-twelves should avoid caffeine and twelve to eighteens may have a hundred milligrams. The ministry also says it collects no data on either side of that line.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · A Week Without Data
stories.headline: Oil jumped four per cent and yields fell anyway
stories.dek: One scheduled American release landed all week. So the long end was priced by a missile strike and a term premium at a twelve-year high, not by anything a statistician published.

stories.headline: Train at your best hour. It changes nothing
stories.dek: The claim every wearable sells finally got a double-blind trial, and the answer rounds to zero. The paper that delivered it cannot keep its own dropout count straight.

stories.headline: Every November sumo ticket is gone, and there is no door
stories.dek: Each row below was put back to a promoter, a venue or an official box office. Two of the biggest names in the window publish no price at all, and one festival has not announced itself.
